title: ACA s. 23 — Statements of claim and defence

content.overview: Section 23 governs the claimant's statement of the facts supporting the claim, points at issue and relief sought, and the respondent's defence, together with the statutory timing and amendment framework.
content.glance: Section 23 governs the claimant's statement of the facts supporting the claim, points at issue and relief sought, and the respondent's defence, together with the statutory timing and amendment framework.
content.study:
Module 1: Pleadings in arbitration
The claim statement identifies facts, issues and relief; the defence responds to those matters. The tribunal may permit amendments subject to the statutory limits.

Module 2: Documentary material
Statements should identify the factual and legal foundation on which the party relies and be supported by the material required by the tribunal's procedural directions.

Module 3: Application
A party should not use amendment as a means of introducing a materially new case in a manner inconsistent with the statutory or procedural framework.

examples.title: Rule applies
examples.body: A claimant sets out the transaction, breach, relief and supporting material; the respondent addresses each material allegation.

examples.title: Rule fails or changes
examples.body: A party introduces a wholly new claim through an amendment after the statutory/procedural stage without establishing why the amendment should be allowed.

hypotheticals.question: What is the function of section 23?
hypotheticals.analysis: It structures the claim and defence, identifies the issues for arbitration and provides the statutory framework for amendments and response.

rows.left: Sets out claim facts, issues and relief.
rows.right: Responds to the claim and states the defence.
